text:
sara: Heads-up — customer (AcmeAnalytics) hit a pretty confusing failure on the reranking endpoint and they blame our console/cURL examples. They sent this: 

oliver: (forwarding their support ticket) 

> "We followed the reranking cURL example on the docs and got back all zeros for scores. No HTTP error, just scores: [0,0,0]. Also sometimes we see a 400 when candidates are > 50. We tried the console example too and it formatted the candidates as a single string. Can you reproduce?"

sara: Repro steps I ran quickly:
1) Copy-paste of the failing curl from docs (exact):
```bash
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  --data-binary '{"query":"best pizza in SF","candidates":"Margherita\nPepperoni\nSicilian"}'
```
This returns 200 with scores [0,0,0] in my run. If I hit with more than 50 candidates I got a 400: "candidates list too long".

matt: Ugh — I think the docs example uses `--data-binary` without setting `Content-Type: application/json` and also accidentally shows candidates as a newline-separated string in the sample, not a JSON array. That would make the server parse candidates as a single string, and our reranker treats non-array candidates as an edge case and returns zeros.

jia: Quick ML note: The model returns low/zero-ish scores when the scorer receives unexpected tokenization shape (we guard for type mismatch but we currently coerce to a fallback path that yields a flat zero vector; should add better error). Also top_k limit: backend config is 50 for single-request rerank (we cap to avoid a huge quadratic cost). Docs currently say 100 in one example — mismatch.

sara: I reproduced both problems: (1) formatting mismatch from docs -> candidates as string (2) docs show top_k: 100 but API caps at 50 -> if user passes >50 we return 400.

oliver: Customer is blocked — they were batching 200 candidates locally expecting rerank to trim to top 100. They hit billing alarms and rate spikes when retrying. Can we give them an immediate workaround?

sara: Workaround I sent them: properly format JSON and set Content-Type header; split into multiple requests or use our Dedicated pipeline for large rerank. Example I gave them: 
```bash
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  --data '{
    "query": "best pizza in SF",
    "candidates": ["Margherita","Pepperoni","Sicilian"],
    "top_k": 20
  }'
```
This returns sensible scores for me locally.

support-bot: Ticket SUP-2026 created for the customer (AcmeAnalytics). Priority: P2.

matt: I'll patch the docs ASAP — two fixes: ensure curl examples include `-H "Content-Type: application/json"` and change the sample candidates to an explicit JSON array. Also update the max top_k to 50 in docs and add a note about server-side cap. I'll open a PR and link here (DOCS-1298).

jia: On the ML side I'll add a defensive error response when input types are wrong (400 with message explaining expected array). Currently the fallback-zero behavior is confusing. Ticket ML-447 opened.

sara: I also asked Customer Success (oliver) to confirm whether they were using the web console quick-run which auto-filled candidates as newline text. 

oliver: Confirmed — they used the console paste box. Console currently accepts both newline text and JSON array, but the client-side sends newline text without converting to array. I'll file a console bug: CON-302. Suggestion for immediate fix: detect newline text and convert to array client-side before sending; but we should surface a UI warning until we change server behavior.

matt: Agree. I'll update the console docs snippet and add an explicit note above the rerank examples: "Candidates must be a JSON array of strings; do not pass newline-separated text."

sara: Customer wanted repro steps so I attached the failing curl (above) and the fixed curl (above) plus a small Node snippet: 
```js
// node repro (works)
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    query: 'best pizza in SF',
    candidates: ['Margherita','Pepperoni','Sicilian']
  })
});
console.log(await res.json());
```

support-bot: Note logged: customer-observed-zero-scores. Linked SUP-2026 -> DOCS-1298 -> ML-447 -> CON-302.

jia: One more detail — if they were hitting 200 candidates and we returned 400, they probably retried rapidly and triggered rate limits. Recommend adding a short note in support reply about exponential backoff and splitting requests to avoid billing/regression spikes.

sara: Sent a reply to customer with: corrected curl, Node snippet, top_k limit (50), backoff guidance, and an ETA for docs fix (ETA: 2 business days). They confirmed it's unblocked for now.

oliver: Customer appreciated the quick fix. They'll hold on larger batch tests until docs/console fixes land.

matt: I'll link PR here when ready. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2317)

sara: Thanks team. Action items:
- matt: patch docs + console snippets (DOCS-1298)
- jia: change ML behavior to 400 on bad input and add diagnostic message (ML-447)
- oliver: console bug + quick client-side fix (CON-302)
- sara: close support ticket once docs PR merged and customer confirms final tests

matt: tagging for follow-up @jia @oliver :thumbsup:

jia: Ack, will take it today.

support-bot: Thread closed by sara (support) — 1769024789
